svg.aria-label: Ten-layer HDI stack-up and via structures
svg.text: Every signal layer has a ground plane directly above and directly below it. That is the constraint the layer count is bought to satisfy, and it is what makes the routing rules short.
Geometry below is a first-pass closed-form calculation. The fabricator's field solver and a TDR coupon set the final widths — the targets are what you hold them to.
GND — reference for L3 and L5
GND — reference for L6 and L8
Copper: 12 µm base + plating on the outer layers (≈30 µm finished),
17 µm on inner signal and ground, 35 µm on the two power layers.
Laminate: mid-Dk, spread-glass, Df ≤ 0.02 at 1 GHz. At 27 mm of trace,
loss is irrelevant; glass-weave skew and Dk consistency are not.
2+6+2: microvias on L1–L3 and L8–L10, mechanical drilling through the six-layer core
Ø0.100 mm laser, 0.250 mm capture pad, copper filled
and plated over. Dimple ≤ 25 µm. This is what puts a
via inside a 0.5 mm-pitch BGA land.
The second hop reaches the first routable layer.
Staggered by ≥ 0.20 mm rather than stacked — stacked
microvias concentrate strain at the target-pad
Ø0.20 mm mechanical, drilled and plated in the
six-layer core before the build-up layers go on.
Ø0.20 mm, 5.3:1. Ground stitching, the thermal
array, and anything outside the fine-pitch fields.
Cheapest structure on the board — use it wherever it
WHY TEN LAYERS AND NOT EIGHT
Propagation delay: 5.2 ps/mm on L1 and L10, 6.6 ps/mm on L3 and L8.
Use it to convert every length-matching rule into the picoseconds
Four signal layers is the floor.
DDR3L ×16 needs two, the 12-net RGMII group needs one it
can keep away from DDR3L, and the outer two are consumed
by component lands and BGA escape before any routing
Every signal layer wants two ground neighbours.
Four signal layers therefore pull in four ground planes.
That is eight. The two power layers make ten.
Eight layers is possible, and worse.
It costs one signal layer its second ground reference,
which puts DDR3L data or RGMII next to a split power
plane. On a 27 mm board the saving is a few dollars; the
The thin L4–L5 and L6–L7 cores are deliberate.
75 µm gives roughly 70 pF of plane capacitance on the core
rail — worth having above 100 MHz, and no substitute for
TDR, not a calculated certificate. One coupon per
impedance class per panel, reported with the lot.
IPC-6012 Class 2 allows 0.75 %. A 9.5 mm 0.5 mm-pitch BGA
does not. Say 0.5 % on the drawing and expect to pay for
Filled and capped to IPC-4761 Type VII.
Copper fill, not conductive paste, on every via inside a
IPC-6012 Class 2 with the microvia addendum, plus
thermal-shock or IST data if any microvia ends up stacked
Flat enough for 0.5 mm pitch. Require a black-pad control
